title: Broken Windows, Open Doors

beats.what: Boyd learns Father Khatri is dead and immediately separates from Kenny, citing something important to do -- the forest departure is imminent
Boyd escorts Sara at gunpoint, warns her the only reason she is alive is because Khatri believed she could help
Jim pitches the radio tower to Donna; she agrees after listing 14 dead Colony House residents, framing the tower as using what is left of the house
Boyd intercepts Abby, Tom, and Eli at gunpoint on the road and convinces them to shelter in town, citing imminent death
Tabitha tells Julie the truth about Thomas's death -- he rolled off the changing table in a one-second distraction
Town residents demand to expel Colony House guests; Kenny faces his first crowd-control test as acting sheriff
Kenny delivers a blistering speech pushing Boyd to go, telling him the town needs him to find answers while Kenny holds things together
Boyd and Kenny say goodbye; Boyd departs with Sara for the forest

character_beats.beat: Wants to leave for the forest immediately; defers again to manage the post-Colony House crisis, but Kenny's confrontational speech forces the departure by reframing delay as cowardice, not duty
Spent prior episodes deferring to Boyd; here he refuses Boyd's hesitation and demands Boyd go, absorbing the sheriff role under visible emotional strain
Wants to protect Julie from adult pain; confesses Thomas's death and her own guilt under pressure from Julie's direct questions, cracking the family's silence
Wants to build the tower despite resource scarcity; negotiates use of Colony House with Donna by meeting her grief directly rather than selling optimism

key_lines.line: The only reason you're alive is because Father Khatri
key_lines.why: Sets the transactional stakes of Sara's survival -- her value is contingent on utility, not mercy
Thomas's death named as the fracture point; the divorce is a symptom, not the cause, reorienting Julie's arc

key_lines.line: Those talismans were a Band-Aid, a temporary reprieve.
key_lines.why: Kenny's speech strips the false security the season built; Colony House breach proves the town was never safe
Boyd and Kenny's farewell; spare and loaded -- the closest Boyd gets to fatherly acknowledgment across eight episodes

open_loops: Who is Abby, the military woman Boyd rescues on the road, and how does she and her family connect to the town's existing power structure?
What did Victor say was starting -- and what does Julie's Farway Tree emergence in the root cellar mean for finding him?
Will the buried basement wires lead to a physical power source, or to something else entirely?
What does Boyd plan to actually do once he reaches the deep forest -- what is his specific goal?

payoffs.what: Julie emerges from the Farway Tree in a root cellar cabinet, paying off Victor's instruction; she reports Victor said it was starting and pushed her in
The Parkinson's disclosure to Kenny from E06 is now active: Boyd uses it to justify the departure timeline when Kenny resists

contradiction.wants: To be a leader who puts others first -- he keeps delaying the forest expedition to manage the town's crises
contradiction.does: Is pushed out the door by his own deputy, who argues that staying is itself a failure of leadership

tone_notes: The opening 4 minutes of credited content are the episode's busiest: minute 8 hits 189 words and minutes 10-14 average 150+, reflecting the post-massacre triage. Then a 142-second silence from 04:26 to 06:48 (the episode's longest, crossing minutes 4-6 at density 4, 0, 0) separates the immediate crisis from the calmer problem-solving scenes. A second 86-second drop at minute 39-40 (density 4, 0) lands during the late-night quiet before Kenny's morning speech. The density profile is an emergency-then-exhale-then-reckoning shape: loud start, long hush, slow build, climactic Kenny speech at minute 34-35 (201, 176) which are the episode's peak.
